title: Finitely many elements of a separably generated extension lie in a finite separable extension of a finitely generated purely transcendental subfield
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and let $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ be a transcendence basis of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that $K$ is separable algebraic over the subfield $k(x_i;i\in I)\subseteq K$ generated by $k$ and all $x_i$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Let $n\ge0$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$. Then there is a finite subset $T\subseteq I$ with the following property: writing $L=k(x_i;i\in T)\subseteq K$ for the subfield generated by $k$ and the $x_i$ with $i\in T$, and $K'=L(a_1,\dots,a_n)\subseteq K$ for the subfield generated by $L$ and $a_1,\dots,a_n$, the extension $K'/L$ is finite (that is, $K'$ is a finite-dimensional $L$-vector space) and separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 030U (lemma-separable-extension-preserves-reducedness, label line 10152), second paragraph, lines 10187-10191: 'For any finite set of elements $\lambda_j\in K$ there exists a finite subset $T\subset I$ such that $k(\{x_i\}_{i\in T})\subset k(\{x_i\}_{i\in T}\cup\{\lambda_j\})$ is finite separable', stated there without proof; tag 030U verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (line 3961)
